The first time I saw Monster Train being played was on Jorbs' Twitch Stream. At first glance I was irritated by the over-the-top graphic and monster design. I found it way too "Hearthstone-y".
But... but - the more I watched it, the more I got hooked, and when I finally bought it, I got absolutely immersed in this bizarre world and its gameplay cycle.
Slay the Spire may have better balancing and more difficult draft decisions in general. But when it comes to pure fun (like the kind of fun when you were playing with water pistols as a child and pretended to be some kind of badass) yes, Monster Train is EXTREMELY fun. There are so many ways to alter your deck, copy cards, remove cards, make certain cards cost 0, double their effectiveness, give them multistrike... Monster Train encourages you to be as ridicilous as possible, because, in the end, this will be the only way to beat the Seraph.

Get it. Play it. And don't take it too seriously.

Rogue like card builder ala Slay the Spire, Rogue Book, etc. 
I havent sunk near as much time in to it as I have others of its kind but already I can say that it's missing some of the charm and it feels a bit bloated. It's not a bad game and honestly if I hadnt played others like the two I mentioned above I may enjoy it even more. I personally feel that it spent more effort on trying to separate itself from the others with a wide range of game mechanics that it forgot to focus on fun. 
HOWEVER, I got it on sale for under $5 so for that I am satisfied and will continue to try it out. Who knows, maybe I will update my review after I have had more time with it.

Was looking for smth on the level of Slay the Spire, and this is WAY too easy for me. It's a good game, but it's far too easy to get overpowered, and only the final boss has any resemblance of difficulty.
Very enjoyable and its so easy to get into and chill out with. Whilst also having competitive aspects in terms of multiplayer. I couldnt recommend this game enough.
Honestly incredibly fun and easy to understand. Beats hearthstone and Legends of runeterra, at least I don't have to pay anything and this game is already a steal for its price.

Definitely my favourite rogue-like card game. The sheer number of decks that you can come up with even between the same two clans selected multiple times over ensures amazing replayability. Combined with the fact that there are now 6 clans to pick from, each with two champions that greatly alter your playstyle, makes it very hard to say that you're always going to be finding something new to try out.

This scratches the itch that Slay the Spire gives you. I've got hundreds of hours in StS both modded and unmodded and I've just begun to uncover what Monster Train has to offer. Can't wait to see what modded content there is after unlocking everything on normal first. Give it a go, especially in sale time.
I have played a lot of slay the spire, this feels a lot like it but still does things in it's own way.

Great game, in the same vein as Slay the Spire. "Feels" shorter because each battle is like five minutes, and each run is less than an hour. You die lots in the beginning, learn the mechanics, start to see synergies, and then slowly get better over time.

If you're expecting a long and satisfying single-player campaign, you don't have that; instead, you have multiple smaller campaigns for each of the factions (some of which unlock over time) and their combinations (each of which has interesting synergies).

If you like slay the spire, this game exceeds that game and I LOVE slay the spire. So many combinations and unique abilities makes every run completely different and more fun. I hope they make more DLC
Slay the Spire but enough different to make it worth your time. Great production values.
Oldukça güzel tasarlanmış, keyifli bir oyun. İçinde kaybolacağınız türden değil ama yeterince de çeşitlilik içeriyor. Kart ve stratejiden keyif alıyorsanız kesinlikle deneyin.

This game is fantastic for card game lovers like my self so i just wanted to give this game a Thumbs Up 👍review.

I'm not gonna tell you how its built as a card battler game with a mix of summoning minion/spell to repel an invading force trying to destroy your train.

I'm not gonna mention how much variation this game gives you each run, with 5 unique factions, each with 2 unique heroes to chose from and you always bring 2 factions each run with a mixed deck/cards every time.

And i'm not even gonna bore you with how damn addictive this game can be, with that good "just one more run before bed" feel.

You just have to pick up this great game your self and find out on your own. Peace! 🤘

Honestly a really amazing deck-building game, with lots of cards to unlock, mutliple card skins and multiple factions.
And who doesn't love trains?

The overall game is really great but what has kept me playing this is the Hellrush feature to actually play along with others. I would love if this would be expended a bit more in the future (e.g. looking at others decks at end of run, etc).
I would recommend to any fans of Slay the Spire. The game play is different as you play with multiple units across three floors instead of with one hero, but it scratches the same itch.
Excellent, well polished deckbuilding game with some unique ideas and TONS of long-lasting content (even withhout DLCs). In some ways this is an evolution of "Slay The Spire".

People have talked about this as the new Slay the Spire. But it's really not. It's fine, for around 20 hours, and then its lack of depth becomes clear.

The reason I say this is that I see a lot pf people leave reviews after having played for 5ish hours, and I don't think those players have had enough experience to really share a fair assessment of the game.

I honestly think it's fine for its price, and as long as you don't expect more than 20ish hours of fun, I would recommend it. But don't expect too much.

Monster Train is one of those card games that starts off light then builds into an immersive experience of strategy, luck, and good times. The game offers a simple introductory game mode that allows newer players to the game, or genre, to get their feet wet. Ongoing progression through a difficulty system that levels up on each game victory adds continual replayability testing various deck combinations and strategies.

Lady luck makes an appearance as additional cards added to the deck throughout each run vary; not only by selected deck combinations, but also by type (spell or minion) and selection.

TLDR; if you're into games like Slay the Spire, this is a must have addition to your collection.
This is like Yu-Gi-Oh and Plants vs Zombies in a mix. The tactics are fun to create and I would recommend this game to folks that are fans of strategy and card battler games.

This is a really fun deckbuilding roguelike at a nice price, I probably would recommend waiting until it is on sale.
If you enjoy Slay The Spire or Inscryption, this is in that same vein. It has a lot more variance than the aforementioned games but you can customize your deck a lot more.
You choose a primary clan and secondary clan, which function similar to a "class" system, and you can get cards from both classes during your run.
I really enjoy it, but the variance is a blessing and a curse. Each run feels very unique but sometimes it just doesn't go your way and the game hits you with a level you aren't prepared for.
There is a large emphasis on balancing big upgrades that also increase enemy difficulty, so you need to carefully decide if you need the power-level increase or keep the enemies weaker.

If you enjoy Roguelike deckbuilders, I highly recommend this one.
Amazing game, excellent graphics and music, together with an amazing progression system that allows for deep strategy with tons of replayability. This is just so incredibly fun!!
A lovely card game that is one part deckbuilder and one part tower defense. Fans of Slay the Spire will enjoy this!
This game is incredible. Very addicting, you will spend lots of time thinking of what to do next while not stressing yourself out, it's the perfect level of complexity. This makes time fly so beware.

It's better than Slay The Spire. It's also different enough - More fun, quicker feeling games, more experimentation and less risk, and I'd expect to put at least another 35 hours in before I even consider myself ready for something different. The power up/buffs are varied and enjoyable to play with and every new formation changes up the game just enough. Heartily recommend.

Biggest reason why i recommend this game is that, unlike many of its contemporaries, i don't feel like i am constantly shafted by RNG, with no way of alleviating these situations or conditions.

There is difficulty, but it doesn't feel like the game is constantly spitting on you and laughing at you.

In other words, this game feels fair even when it is hard and beats you.

This game exemplified errors and improvements for Slay the Spire that i didnt even know it needed. I've had steam for a very long time and this is the first review I have ever given because it feels wrong to not give it a perfect score.

Endless combinations and possibilities and it feels fresh every single run I play. If you liked Slay the Spire a little bit, you will absolutely love this game.

For me, the only con is that I wish there was more DLC.
It's kind of fun but not as fun as Slay the Spire. It was too easy to beat in just one run. However, the game is quite charming and I'd recommend to get it on sale.
Pretty good mix of card/team roguelikes. Nothing more to say just good and fun give it a go if you like any of those genres :3
Good game, very fun. I am also fan of Slay the Spire and I like this game too. I do think they are different thought. Still recommend. Thumbs up. :)

Yeah it's a dang solid game there bud. Not the number one best in the genre of crawly card battlers, but undeniably pretty darn good in pretty much every regard.

Not a huge fan of the art personally, looks a bit like a mobile game, but it's not bad enough to detract from the experience. Music is fair but doesn't slap.

The core gameplay loop is very solid, the different factions and keyword mechanics are a ton of fun to mix and match, and every run gives you enough progression to feel rewarded until you're hooked.

So it's like a 7.5, maybe 8/10? A-Tier, not S-Tier, but if you like the genre it's worth the admission fee.

reviewing this in excitement for monster train 2 coming out
in comparison to games similar to itself the game has polish, but honestly the game play has it flaws,
now with the last divinity dlc on the other hand, giving you the ability to take rewards in exchange for permanently buffing enemies over the course of the run, giving you the ability to mash two units together and create a Frankenstein, giving you a second leader for each faction, while the game play still has its flaws with dlc included it truly did at an impressive amount of game play variation while if you've never played a rouge-like card i would still recommend slay the spire as its the paragon of its genre this game holds its own and is unique enough where i would recommend playing it its a good game and i cant wait for the upgraded sequel to come out

Description: (Non-Early-Access) Roguelike-Card-Battler with a lot of depth, a ton of things to unlock and multiple strategies & deck archetypes. If you like Slay-The-Spire you will love this.

Positive (+)

+ Easy to grasp the fundamental game mechanics & Smooth introduction of additional features

+ Huge complexity & depth once you unlock more cards & deck types

+ Multiplayer custom challenges, daily challenges, leaderboards

+ The amount of unlockables is really high and feels motiviating

+ Different characters & allied clans bring a lot of variety options to choose from when beginning a new run

Neutral (>)

> The soundtrack is fitting & accompanies the different levels & bosses individually

Negative (-)

- No steam-workshop support (yet)

- An art-style which you need to get used to. I do not like it (hugely subjective though)

Overall: If you like slay the spire or card-battlers in general this game is a no brainer. HUGE replay value and a lot of fun. Even though I do not like the art style this should not stop you from buying and enjoying this game. If you are unsure, try the game. A full run takes you about ~1hours15minutes. So can still get a refund. I doubt you would want this after playing the game though. The game is a 10/10 in the card-battle genre!

Edit* There is a demo!

I like deckbuilders but I don't really love them to play for hundred of hours but for whatever reasons this game is the only thing I can think of for the last 2 weeks, it's like something just clicked and now I understand the game, going from Cov 7 to 16 without much troubles.
Honestly I prefer this over StS because this game is like a power fantasy especially with the DLC, you gain so much power after every battle, a run only consist of 8-9 battles, so many playstyles, most of the cards are either good or amazing value, UI/UX are great with controller, totally worth buying.
My hope for the sequel is for it to do just as good and with different strategies.
Edit:
100% achievements, beaten Divinity Cov 25 with 5 clans, can't wait for the sequel.

I love this game. I tried it on a whim on a weekend when I had a buddy over. Needless to say we binged it all night for 3 nights straight and im still excited to play more. 10/10 game. Cards have great synergy with each other and the developers put a lot of thought into making this game. THANK YOU SHINY SHOE!
Very interesting card strategy game with fun and varied mechanics. The music is meh, but still a great game overall.
Amazing game, carried the torch forward from slay the spire and added a lot more to the genre. 10/10

slay the spire but with more fun. better graphics, and less frustration
The game offers really fun combos
perfect if you have 30 minutes in front of you

very cool but missing opportunity for Monster Big Rig
would very much enjoy hauling my crucible in a Kenworth or Western Star®
i didn't know running a train could be so difficult tho i will be more grateful next time i ride one
I've played many rogue-like deck-builder games before. Monster Train easily made it into my top 3 favorite deck-builders. I love this game!

Put simply, this is the most fun I've had with a deck builder. It has a looser design than something like Slay the Spire, but it has a much greater variety of possible builds as a result.

The main single player mode has 20 possible combinations of primary and secondary clans, and there are 25 Covenant ranks to climb, each with higher and higher difficulty. I am currently at Covenant 10 and I can see that it will take a lot more practice to progress further.

The Daily Challenge and Challenge modes have a selection of interesting and entertaining modifiers available, and I have enjoyed the few I have tackled so far.

Hell Rush, the multiplayer mode, is also very fun and a surprisingly fresh approach. You are placed in a lobby with a handful of others and much work against strict time limits to clear each combat encounter with the same initial setup as your competitors. If you die, you are dropped from the competition. If you run out of time, the combat will auto-resolve from that point on, meaning you can play no more cards and must hope your units last on their own. Succeed, and you will be competing for score with the remaining competitors.

Simply put, if you enjoy deck builders and roguelites, this is more than worth your money.

Every Thanksgiving, the Monster Train tries to get back to the center of Hell and relight the pyre.

This is their story.

Wow, I've played over 200 hours of this game and it is one of my all-time favourites, and somehow I haven't reviewed it yet...

So, do I recommend it? HELL YEAH I DO!

Great game. Plays like a direct sequel to Slay the Spire, but that's fine because I loved Slay the Spire. This makes several improvements to good ol' STS:
- More engaging combat
- More varied starting decks
- More varied upgrade options for drafted cards

Overall I'm enjoying it a lot. Thanks to the devs for a great game.

Much easier to understand that you would expect for a game about building a demon infused deck of cards to defend a tripple decker train from a band of over zealous angels.

The core game play is varied, challenging, rewarding and at times incredibly silly which is exactly what I look for in a roguelike. I can see myself popping back to this game for the occasional train ride.

If you like Slay the spire, Izac or Hades you will likely like this game too

This is one of the all time greats. I am not sure why the Dev's dropped this as they could have made way more money with a few DLC's and map/boss expansions. Thankfully the community has built some really good mods which extend the life of the game dramatically. I would argue at the higher ends of difficulty it can be more challenging than Slay the Spire. Hopefully the devs see STS2 coming out and decide to bring Monster Train 2 out... Perhaps this time from the good guys perspective? If you own STS and not this just buy the base game and try it out.. Huge amounts of fun!!
Great game! Lots of fun! Wish there was loads more content so I could keep enjoying the game more!
Amazing game! The theme, ui, monsters, and gameplay are unique and fun. Be warned, each run can take over an hour though, which is my only gripe.
It's fun. Music is average, it looks like a mobile game, it's easy to pick up and play. I would say wait for a sale because it's not the best game I've played, but still a fun game.

Best roguelite card battler I've played to date. Yes, I'd rank it above Slay the Spire personally.

I tend to lose motivation for these games once I've unlocked everything. This game took considerably longer to do so that most in the genre.

Complaints are few and spread across different topics, so no single problem stands out.
